pack.title: Acme Shop microservice architecture standards
pack.description: Engineering rules every Acme Shop service design, configuration and container image must follow. Checked against ADRs, application configuration and Dockerfiles.

rules.title: No shared database between services
rules.requirement: Each microservice owns its data. No service reads or writes another service's database, schema, tables or replicas; data is shared only through APIs or events.

decider.topic: which database, schema or tables a service owns, reads or writes
decider.question: How does this text describe data access between services?

owns-own-data.description: each service reads and writes only its own database; other data comes through APIs or events

accesses-other-service-data.description: a service reads or writes another service's database, tables, schema or replica directly

not-discussed.description: the text does not discuss how services access data

rules.fix_hint: Replace direct table access with the owning service's API or with events it publishes.

rules.title: Reliable event publishing
rules.requirement: When a service changes state and publishes an event about it, both must succeed or fail together, for example with a transactional outbox. Publishing after commit without a delivery guarantee is not allowed.

decider.topic: a service publishing its own events or messages after changing its own data (not consuming events from others)
decider.question: How does this text make sure events are not lost when a service changes state and publishes an event?

guaranteed.description: the state change and the outgoing event are committed together (transactional outbox, change data capture or equivalent)

not-guaranteed.description: the event or message is sent only after the database commit, or fire-and-forget, so if sending fails or the service crashes the event is lost, skipped or only logged

not-discussed.description: the text does not describe publishing events

rules.fix_hint: Write the event to an outbox table in the same transaction and relay it to the broker.

rules.title: No secrets in configuration files
rules.requirement: Passwords, API keys and tokens never appear as literal values in configuration files. They are resolved at runtime from Vault or environment variables.
rules.fix_hint: Move the value to Vault and reference it, e.g. password: ${vault:secret/billing/db#password}.

rules.title: Correlation ID on every inter-service message
rules.requirement: Every message and request between services carries a correlation ID so a business process can be traced end to end.

decider.topic: messages, events or requests sent between services, or how they are traced
decider.question: Does this text say that messages or requests between services carry a correlation ID or trace ID?

carries-correlation-id.description: messages or requests between services carry a correlation ID or trace ID, for example an X-Correlation-Id header with the business key

no-correlation-id.description: messages or requests between services are described without any correlation or trace ID, or tracing is explicitly left out

not-discussed.description: the text does not describe messages or requests between services

rules.fix_hint: Add a correlationId header to every message and propagate it on outgoing calls.

rules.title: Synchronous calls declare timeouts and a fallback
rules.requirement: Every synchronous call to another service sets a timeout and defines what happens when the call fails or times out (retry with limit, fallback or compensation).

decider.topic: a request/response call (for example HTTP or REST) that one service makes to another service or to an external provider's API
decider.question: How does this text handle failures of synchronous calls to other services?

timeout-and-fallback.description: synchronous calls have a stated timeout and a stated retry limit, fallback or compensation

missing-timeout-or-fallback.description: a call to another service or an external service (for example over HTTP) is described without a stated timeout, or without saying what happens when it fails

not-discussed.description: the text does not describe synchronous calls to other services

rules.fix_hint: Set an explicit client timeout and a bounded retry with a fallback or compensation step.

rules.title: Health endpoint exposed
rules.requirement: Every Spring Boot service exposes the actuator health endpoint so the platform can probe it.
rules.fix_hint: Keep health in management.endpoints.web.exposure.include (or leave it unset: Spring Boot exposes health by default) and do not exclude or disable it.

rules.title: Pinned container base images
rules.requirement: Container images build from a pinned base image version, never from the latest tag or an untagged image.
rules.fix_hint: Pin the base image to an explicit version, e.g. eclipse-temurin:21.0.4_7-jre.

yaml:
# Acme Shop architecture rules, a custom rule pack.
# Every pack follows src/shodhaka/rules/rulepack.schema.json; DORA and ISO packs use the same shape.
pack: acme-architecture
version: "1.0"
title: Acme Shop microservice architecture standards
description: >
  Engineering rules every Acme Shop service design, configuration and container image must follow.
  Checked against ADRs, application configuration and Dockerfiles.

rules:
  - id: ARCH-01
    title: No shared database between services
    severity: high
    applies_to: [adr]
    requirement: >
      Each microservice owns its data. No service reads or writes another service's
      database, schema, tables or replicas; data is shared only through APIs or events.
    decider:
      topic: which database, schema or tables a service owns, reads or writes
      question: How does this text describe data access between services?
      options:
        owns-own-data:
          verdict: compliant
          description: each service reads and writes only its own database; other data comes through APIs or events
        accesses-other-service-data:
          verdict: gap
          description: a service reads or writes another service's database, tables, schema or replica directly
        not-discussed:
          verdict: not_applicable
          description: the text does not discuss how services access data
    fix_hint: Replace direct table access with the owning service's API or with events it publishes.

  - id: ARCH-02
    title: Reliable event publishing
    severity: high
    applies_to: [adr]
    requirement: >
      When a service changes state and publishes an event about it, both must succeed or fail
      together, for example with a transactional outbox. Publishing after commit without a
      delivery guarantee is not allowed.
    decider:
      topic: a service publishing its own events or messages after changing its own data (not consuming events from others)
      question: How does this text make sure events are not lost when a service changes state and publishes an event?
      options:
        guaranteed:
          verdict: compliant
          description: the state change and the outgoing event are committed together (transactional outbox, change data capture or equivalent)
        not-guaranteed:
          verdict: gap
          description: the event or message is sent only after the database commit, or fire-and-forget, so if sending fails or the service crashes the event is lost, skipped or only logged
        not-discussed:
          verdict: not_applicable
          description: the text does not describe publishing events
    fix_hint: Write the event to an outbox table in the same transaction and relay it to the broker.

  - id: ARCH-03
    title: No secrets in configuration files
    severity: high
    applies_to: [config]
    requirement: >
      Passwords, API keys and tokens never appear as literal values in configuration files.
      They are resolved at runtime from Vault or environment variables.
    deterministic:
      check: secret_scan
    fix_hint: "Move the value to Vault and reference it, e.g. password: ${vault:secret/billing/db#password}."

  - id: ARCH-04
    title: Correlation ID on every inter-service message
    severity: medium
    applies_to: [adr]
    requirement: >
      Every message and request between services carries a correlation ID so a business
      process can be traced end to end.
    decider:
      topic: messages, events or requests sent between services, or how they are traced
      scope: document  # one section stating the correlation ID covers the whole design
      question: Does this text say that messages or requests between services carry a correlation ID or trace ID?
      options:
        carries-correlation-id:
          verdict: compliant
          description: messages or requests between services carry a correlation ID or trace ID, for example an X-Correlation-Id header with the business key
        no-correlation-id:
          verdict: gap
          description: messages or requests between services are described without any correlation or trace ID, or tracing is explicitly left out
        not-discussed:
          verdict: not_applicable
          description: the text does not describe messages or requests between services
    fix_hint: Add a correlationId header to every message and propagate it on outgoing calls.

  - id: ARCH-05
    title: Synchronous calls declare timeouts and a fallback
    severity: medium
    applies_to: [adr]
    requirement: >
      Every synchronous call to another service sets a timeout and defines what happens when
      the call fails or times out (retry with limit, fallback or compensation).
    decider:
      topic: a request/response call (for example HTTP or REST) that one service makes to another service or to an external provider's API
      question: How does this text handle failures of synchronous calls to other services?
      options:
        timeout-and-fallback:
          verdict: compliant
          description: synchronous calls have a stated timeout and a stated retry limit, fallback or compensation
        missing-timeout-or-fallback:
          verdict: gap
          description: a call to another service or an external service (for example over HTTP) is described without a stated timeout, or without saying what happens when it fails
        not-discussed:
          verdict: not_applicable
          description: the text does not describe synchronous calls to other services
    fix_hint: Set an explicit client timeout and a bounded retry with a fallback or compensation step.

  - id: ARCH-06
    title: Health endpoint exposed
    severity: medium
    applies_to: [config]
    requirement: >
      Every Spring Boot service exposes the actuator health endpoint so the platform can probe it.
    deterministic:
      check: health_endpoint
    fix_hint: "Keep health in management.endpoints.web.exposure.include (or leave it unset: Spring Boot exposes health by default) and do not exclude or disable it."

  - id: ARCH-07
    title: Pinned container base images
    severity: low
    applies_to: [dockerfile]
    requirement: >
      Container images build from a pinned base image version, never from the latest tag or an untagged image.
    deterministic:
      check: pinned_base_image
    fix_hint: Pin the base image to an explicit version, e.g. eclipse-temurin:21.0.4_7-jre.
